items.text:
**Agree with retained remediation labor, no automatic resume, and no inherited eight-hour phase loss—as a NEW provisional completion.** The finite host-authored consequence fixture is also appropriate; it exercises supplied mishap outcomes without claiming manufacturing, ingredient settlement or mishap selection.

One restriction needs tightening: **“fouled station—new order” must not permit resuming another crafting order merely because its record already exists.**

The [sourced mishap table, lines 84–95](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/9fd32abe010b768119ceae31b837340d431a4a9a/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/CRAFTING_HARVEST_PLAYTEST.md#L84) supports these distinctions:

| Mishap | Remediation | Restriction |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — Spill | One active hour of cleanup | Station unavailable for ordinary productive use. Cleanup itself remains possible. |
| 2 — Miscalibration | Two active hours by someone proficient with the kit; no extra ingredients | Kit cannot support another **crafting check**. This does not itself prohibit research checks. |
| 5 — Fouling | One labor-hour per worker who participated in the failed order; physically capable cleaners may contribute simultaneously | Station cannot support another **crafting order**, including resumption of another order there. It is not automatically a prohibition on every noncrafting activity. |
| 6 — Lost notes | Original lead spends one active hour reconstructing the trade log | Lead cannot begin another crafting order in that trade. Formula ownership remains intact; reconstruction does not retroactively restore the failed order’s denied research XP. |

For result 5, freeze the original participating-worker set in the occurred-event record. Count the lead and actual assistants—not the expedition roster or the later cleanup crew.

**NEW remediation completion details:**

- Retain genuinely performed eligible labor through pause, incapacity and save/resume. Revalidate capability, access and qualifications before explicit resume.
- Credit parallel labor only where expressly supported: result 5. For this first fixture, use serial cleanup for result 1, one designated proficient recalibrator for result 2, and the original lead for result 6. No inferred assistance speedup.
- Count each worker’s interval once. Stop contribution at completion; excess labor is not banked against another incident.
- Track obligations by incident. Completing one remedy clears only that incident’s restriction; cancellation of an assignment does not erase the obligation.
- These fixed-labor remedies have no printed completion check. Once final lawful labor is earned, complete once under the existing boundary sequence, as with copying; do not invent an additional conscious act or roll at the endpoint.

Actual destruction or newly introduced physical damage remains separate from ordinary interruption.

**The proposed object profile is sound with two qualifications.** The [equipment record](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/9fd32abe010b768119ceae31b837340d431a4a9a/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/data/playtest/equipment_acquisition_candidate.json#L3978) confirms `tools.alchemist-s-supplies`, **50 gp and 8 lb**. The [object procedure](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/9fd32abe010b768119ceae31b837340d431a4a9a/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/EQUIPMENT_ACQUISITION_PLAYTEST.md#L165) supplies **5 structural HP** for a tool and requires mixed-object load-bearing material to be established beforehand.

Your wooden case and intact ordinary implements are **TEST_ONLY physical facts**, not recovered catalog composition. Compatible bludgeoning damage is acceptable for that declared object. However, “no special defense” must retain the procedure’s ordinary **poison/psychic immunity**. Mishap 3 directly supplies its damage point; it does not require a Sunder attack roll.

At zero HP, the kit is Broken and loses functional benefits while retaining identity, mass and custody. Consequently, **Broken can prevent research that actually requires a usable kit**, even though Miscalibrated alone does not.

**Structural repair is a separate procedure.** [Repair, lines 207–211](https://github.com/BordelonDevOps/DecenniumDescent/blob/9fd32abe010b768119ceae31b837340d431a4a9a/DescentReviewChanges/ReviewBible/docs/mechanics/EQUIPMENT_ACQUISITION_PLAYTEST.md#L205) requires:

- A relevant trained toolkit and actual workable materials.
- For this ordinary 50-gp, 5-HP kit: **12 gp 5 sp of materials, one active hour, DC 10 tool task check**.
- A recoverable main body when repairing from zero HP.

Alchemy proficiency establishes recalibration eligibility; it does not automatically establish competence and equipment for every wooden/glass/metal repair. A narrow case-only repair can use explicitly supplied relevant tools/training and intact implements. The Broken target cannot supply its own missing functional toolkit benefit.

Repair restores structural HP; it does **not** clear miscalibration, station fouling or lost-log obligations. Recalibration does not restore HP. This remediation completion also does not silently settle structural repair’s material-debit or interruption timing.

Your life-calendar design remains consistent with the adopted policy. Keep the global actual death-save sequence as an audit identity, not the scheduling clock: determine due markers and deterministic equal-time ordering first, then allocate the sequence. Save/resume and mode changes must not create a second save for an already-resolved actor marker.
